title: add-transactional-tenant-seed-controller-and-quiesce-hook-values
author: Nora Patel
release_notes: Adds a transactional tenant-seed controller values schema and optional quiesce-hook scaffolding to enable safe, resumable tenant bootstraps and deterministic graceful quiesce behaviour during upgrades. No breaking changes to existing installs when new values are omitted.
description: Context and motivation: Private installer customers have hit flaky tenant seed runs and race conditions during rolling upgrades when tenant bootstrap jobs are requeued or retried. This PR introduces a values-first approach that wires an opinionated, idempotent tenant-seed controller configuration and a pluggable quiesce-hook scaffold so operators can opt into safe quiesce semantics during upgrades. Goals: (1) Provide a values schema for transactional seed semantics (lease, idempotency, backoff profiles), (2) Add templated quiesce hook that can be enabled per-tenant or cluster-wide, (3) Surface init telemetry toggles so the console and observability stack can correlate seed progress across retries. Changes are behind feature gates and default to backward-compatible behavior. Checklist: - [x] values.schema.json for charts/redwood-private with new top-level keys: seed.transactional, seed.backoffProfiles, quiesce.enabled, quiesce.gracePeriod - [x] templates/init-seed-job.yaml: new controller-driven mode + legacy job compatibility flag - [x] templates/quiesce-hook.yaml: hook template with leader-elector and optional preflight image verification - [x] chart helpers: functions for merging tenant overlays and defaulting backoff profiles - [x] unit tests for values validation and helm template smoke tests - [x] documentation stub in docs/helm/values-tenant-seed.md Related work: ENG-1429 (tenant bootstrap reliability), SUP-7241 (customer incident). Implementation notes: the seed controller config uses a small JSON blob that is translated into annotations on the seed job (leases, opaque id) so existing runners that don't adopt the controller remain functional. The quiesce hook is a lightweight Job template that runs as a pre-upgrade hook when enabled; it performs an idempotent drain + wait-for-kv-ack step and writes a hook-state ConfigMap key to guard rollback/unwind flows. Migration guidance: omitted values will continue to use legacy behavior; enabling "seed.transactional.enabled" triggers the controller-mode which is additive and reversible. See release notes for operational considerations.

notes_for_ops: To enable transactional seed on a cluster set charts.redwood-private.seed.transactional.enabled=true and configure seed.transactional.controllerImage if using the controller mode. If you rely on legacy job names, set seed.legacyJobName to preserve behavior. Quiesce defaults are disabled; enable quiesce.enabled=true for maintenance windows. Observability: enable initTelemetry.enabled=true to emit seed.progress and seed.attempt_count metrics.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. All changes are feature-flagged and default to legacy behavior. Risk arises when operators enable transactional seed without adjusting backoff profiles for very large tenant counts. Recommend canary enabling on a single tenant before cluster-wide rollout.
